thread:
alice: FYI — new onboarding support case. user on a TS + webpack app did `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` and got `undefined`.

alice: they then tried `const SDK = require('redwood-inference')` and `console.log(SDK)` printed `{}` which was super confusing.

tom: ah yep default vs named export + package exports quirks. what bundler config are they on?

alice: webpack 5 with default interop enabled, Babel + ts-loader. they also tried bundling for Bun and got `SyntaxError` from the ESM build.

riley: quick repro we can paste in docs:
```js
// ESM (recommended)
import { Client } from 'redwood-inference'
const c = new Client({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API })

// CJS fallback for legacy apps
const { Client: CjsClient } = require('redwood-inference/cjs')
const c2 = new CjsClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API })
```
iley: also show the bad patterns to avoid: `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` and `const SDK = require('redwood-inference')` (without /cjs) — both are common mistakes.

docs-eng: agreed. propose a short "Interop and bundlers" section in quickstart explaining: (1) we export named symbols (Client, utils), no default export; (2) we publish an ESM primary build + a `/cjs` CJS compatibility entry; (3) we ship an `/edge` ESM-targeted bundle for edge environments.

eng-runtime: we'll double-check package.json `exports` and `types` fields. make sure conditional exports don't accidentally make `require('redwood-inference')` resolve to an ESM-only path in Node versions that still support require. filing RW-runtime-1101 to audit.

alice: feel free to include a tiny diagnostic snippet in docs like: `node -e "console.log(require('redwood-inference/cjs'))"` which should print something like `{ Client: [Function: Client], version: 'x.y.z' }`. that helped the user debug quickly.

tom: TypeScript note for docs: for ESM users: `import type { ClientOptions } from 'redwood-inference'`. for CJS codebases using TS, show JSDoc typedefs: `/** @type {import('redwood-inference').ClientOptions} */ const opts = {}`. and mention `@ts-ignore` only as last resort.

riley: bundler gotchas to call out: webpack may add node-polyfills when requiring CJS — that increases bundle size and can break edge deployments. recommend using the ESM root or `/edge` for Edge (Vercel/Cloudflare/Bun), and ensure `target: 'es2020'` or similar.

docs-eng: I'll author the PR with a 2-row table + examples, plus a short FAQ entry "Why do my imports return {} or undefined?" with quick checks and commands.

eng-runtime: we'll add a CI smoke test (`ci/cjs-smoke.js`) that runs `node` against the CJS entry to assert `typeof Client === 'function'`. also add a lightweight bundler smoke that attempts to build a minimal edge bundle in a container to catch regressions early.

alice: can we also show the package.json minimal `exports` example we expect in docs so that library consumers who publish their own packages learn how to avoid pitfalls? a short snippet: "\"exports\": { \".\": { \"import\": \"./dist/index.mjs\", \"require\": \"./dist/index.cjs\" }, \"./edge\": \"./dist/edge.mjs\" }".

tom: good idea. that helps infra folks and advanced users. also call out `types` pointing to `dist/index.d.ts`.

devx-bot: Created issue RW-DX-1100: "docs(js): interop guide for ESM/CJS/Bundlers + edge bundle guidance" 44d https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1100

docs-eng: I'll open the docs PR today and include the diagnostic commands, TS/JSDoc patterns, and the package.json exports example. can someone add the sample-app smoke tests and tag eng-runtime for the audit?

eng-runtime: adding RW-runtime-1101 and will post results in that issue. we'll also verify our published dist contains both index.mjs and index.cjs and that types are wired.

alice: thanks all 680. small docs + tests should save a lot of onboarding time — i'll paste PR links here when ready.
